$comment: Declared staging for the parity oracle.
The oracle asserts that every admin operation and every operation input field in the hub's
checked-in contract fixture maps to a provider attribute, or carries an explicit unmanaged
reason. The check is asymmetric: an operation the fixture has that the provider lacks fails;
one the provider handles that the fixture lacks is allowed. Asymmetry alone is not enough,
because the fake validates requests against the fixture's input schemas and those set
additionalProperties:false — so a provider-ahead field would be rejected before the
comparison ran, and a blanket exemption for unknowns would make a typo indistinguishable
from intentional staging.
Hence this file. Each entry names an operation or 'operation.field' this provider supports
ahead of the hub's fixture, with the reason. Validation is skipped only for declared
entries; anything else unknown still fails.
An entry the fixture has caught up to must be removed. That expiry check runs only in this
repository's own CI against its own pinned fixture — never from the hub's invocation of the
coverage app — because enforcing it on both sides would deadlock the handoff: the hub could
not land its fixture while the entry was still declared, and this repo could not drop the
entry while its pin was still old.
Landing order is therefore: provider ships support with an entry here; the hub lands its
fixture and implementation; this repo bumps its pin and drops the entry, in one commit.
Currently declared: §23.3's settings pair and §23.6's owner aliases. pmcp_hub_settings
reaches hub_settings_get / hub_settings_update, and both app resources send the optional
typescript_aliases object on app_create / app_update. All four are provider-ahead of the
pinned fixture until the hub's own contracts/admin-ops.json lands them and this pin is
bumped; the expiry rule above then names each entry that must go.
